{
  "root_cause": "The offcanvas plugin always installs a focus-in listener that traps focus inside the element, regardless of the backdrop setting. When the help panel is shown with data-bs-backdrop=\"false\" (non‑modal), this trap prevents tab navigation to fields outside the offcanvas, such as the amount input.",
  "repair_strategy": "Modify the _enforceFocusOnElement method to conditionally install the focus-in listener only when this._config.backdrop is true. This preserves the initial focus on the offcanvas while allowing tab escape when the backdrop is disabled, keeping the panel non‑modal.",
  "edits": [
    {
      "path": "js/src/offcanvas.js",
      "sha256": "acd803008c3e6a0a08baaaad65fc36f204036f14190f4b30ac770f0097cd96b7",
      "before": "  _enforceFocusOnElement(element) {\n    EventHandler.off(document, EVENT_FOCUSIN) // guard against infinite focus loop\n    EventHandler.on(document, EVENT_FOCUSIN, event => {\n      if (document !== event.target &&\n        element !== event.target &&\n        !element.contains(event.target)) {\n        element.focus()\n      }\n    })\n    element.focus()\n  }",
      "after": "  _enforceFocusOnElement(element) {\n    if (this._config.backdrop) {\n      EventHandler.off(document, EVENT_FOCUSIN) // guard against infinite focus loop\n      EventHandler.on(document, EVENT_FOCUSIN, event => {\n        if (document !== event.target &&\n          element !== event.target &&\n          !element.contains(event.target)) {\n          element.focus()\n        }\n      })\n    }\n    element.focus()\n  }"
  }
],
  "expected_accessibility_effect": "Users can tab from the offcanvas help panel into the main form (e.g., to the amount field) when the panel is non‑modal, satisfying the requirement to reach the amount field within six tab presses.",
  "functional_risks": [
    "If an offcanvas instance relies on the focus trap for modal behavior but has backdrop=false due to a misconfiguration, the trap will be disabled, potentially allowing focus to leave unintentionally. However, the condition preserves the trap when backdrop is true, so normal modal offcanvases remain unaffected.",
    "Initial focus still lands on the offcanvas element; users who expect the first tab stop inside the panel may need to press Shift+Tab to return to the trigger button, which is acceptable for a non‑modal panel."
  ],
  "verification_requirements": [
    "After opening the help panel with data-bs-backdrop=\"false\", pressing Tab twice should move focus to the #amount field.",
    "Focus should not be returned to the offcanvas when tabbing out of it.",
    "When data-bs-backdrop=\"true\" (or default), the focus trap must remain active: tabbing inside the offcanvas should not escape.",
    "The Escape key must continue to close the offcanvas regardless of the backdrop setting.",
    "The help panel should remain visible and not be dismissed inadvertently during interaction."
  ]
}

But the observed failure says cannot reach #amount within 6 Tab transitions. Let's examine further. Continuing: Seq4: #amount -> div #help (so after amount, tab goes back to #help) Seq5: #help -> button #help-close Seq6: #help-close -> input #amount ... loops. Thus the tab order is cycling between #help, #help-close, #amount. It never reaches other fields like submit-report etc. But the requirement is just to reach #amount within 6 tabs from start of journey after opening help. Starting point after opening help: focus is on #help (the offcanvas). Then we need to tab to #amount within 6 tabs. Let's count: Starting focus on #help (seq1). Press Tab -> goes to #help-close (seq2). That's 1 tab. Press Tab again -> goes to #amount (seq3). That's 2 tabs. So actually it reaches #amount within 2 tabs. Why did the test fail?
